comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1, C29, C48-C51. Both evaluations find the evidence for AURKA APA isoforms compelling and well-supported through multiple methods (database searches, RT-qPCR, clinical correlation). Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Both address claims C53-C58 regarding differential protein expression of isoforms. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED, but peer reviewers raise UNCERTAIN concerns about generalizability beyond U2OS cells to TNBC, questioning whether findings extend to the clinically relevant context.

Strong agreement on claims C61-C63 regarding similar mRNA stability between isoforms. Both evaluations find this SUPPORTED and accept it as ruling out differential decay as the mechanism, directing focus to translational control.

Strong agreement on claims C66-C68 (overlapping with C4). Both evaluations find the nascent chain IP data SUPPORTED and accept the conclusion that translation is the primary regulatory mechanism. Peer reviewers commend the innovative methodology.

Strong agreement on claims C73-C77 (overlapping with C6-C7). Both evaluations find the C-TRIPS assay data SUPPORTED, demonstrating differential cell cycle regulation of translation between isoforms. Peer reviewers specifically commend the novel methodology.

Strong agreement on claims C83-C90 regarding hsa-let-7a targeting of the long isoform. Both evaluations find evidence SUPPORTED through multiple complementary approaches including miRNA co-transfection, mutation, and inhibitor experiments.

Both address claims C91-C92, C95 regarding phase-specific hsa-let-7a effects. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, peer reviewers also find evidence convincing but Reviewer 3 questions whether translation is more important than transcriptional changes in controlling AURKA during cell cycle.

Both address claims C96-C101 regarding CRISPR mutants. OpenEval finds all claims SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept the mutant generation (C96-C98) but Reviewer 2 raises UNCERTAIN concerns about the CHX experiment interpretation (C100-C101), suggesting proteasome inhibitor would be better.

Strong agreement on claims C102-C105 (overlapping with C8-C9) regarding functional consequences in CRISPR mutants. Both evaluations find the proliferation, colony formation, and migration data SUPPORTED and accept these as demonstrating cancer-relevant phenotypes.

Both address claims C78-C80 regarding constant isoform ratios through cell cycle. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as distinguishing APA from translational regulation. Peer reviewers also accept this finding (SUPPORTED), acknowledging the distinction between mechanisms.

Both address claims C106-C107 regarding SLR as crucial determinant. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on synthesis of multiple experiments. Peer reviewers also find evidence convincing (SUPPORTED), noting it ties together database observations and mechanistic findings.

Both address claims C117-C118, C121 regarding translational elongation mechanism. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on TRIPS and NC IP data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting mechanisms remain 'largely obscure' and suggesting investigation of let-7a expression/activity changes during cell cycle.

Partial overlap on claims C123-C124 regarding phase-specific effects. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning novelty and suggesting further mechanistic investigation of cell cycle-dependent let-7a regulation.

Strong agreement on claims C69-C72 regarding methodological validations. Both evaluations find these control experiments SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly commend the rigorous controls demonstrating reporters work as intended.

Both address claims C52, C65 regarding reporter system controls. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as establishing assay validity. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, noting rigorous control experiments without raising concerns.

OpenEval R12 addresses claims C110-C111 integrating mechanistic findings with functional outcomes, finding SUPPORTED. Peer R9 addresses overlapping functional claims C102-C105, also finding SUPPORTED and noting the data 'nicely tie together' observations.

OpenEval R15 addresses claims C2-C3, C45-C47 establishing clinical context, finding SUPPORTED. Peer R1 addresses overlapping clinical claims C1, C29, C48-C51, also finding SUPPORTED with explicit affirmation of clinical correlations.
OpenEval finds claims C10-C19 (background knowledge) SUPPORTED as appropriately cited. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these background claims.
OpenEval finds claims C20-C25 (knowledge gap framing) SUPPORTED as appropriately establishing study motivation. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these framing claims.

OpenEval finds claims C26-C30 (APA background and AURKA database finding) SUPPORTED. While peer R1 mentions C29, no peer result specifically evaluates this combination of general APA knowledge with the specific AURKA database search.
OpenEval finds claims C31-C36 (APA in cancer background) SUPPORTED as well-cited context. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these background claims.

OpenEval finds claims C37-C44 (miRNA and hsa-let-7a background) SUPPORTED as appropriately cited. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these background claims, though peer reviewers do evaluate the experimental findings on let-7a.
